title: Quality Engineering Manager
description:
Quality Engineering Manager – Manufacturing | Charlotte Metro

About the Company
At TalentBridge, we're representing a long-standing manufacturing client known for their commitment to engineering excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.

This U.S.-based organization designs and manufactures precision-engineered mechanical and electro-mechanical products used in commercial, industrial, and architectural applications. The Monroe, NC facility serves as the North American Center of Excellence for their product line — a well-established, growing operation with a strong culture of teamwork, safety, and quality.
Position Overview
We are seeking a Quality Engineering Manager with a strong drive for continuous improvement and leadership in total quality management.

This individual will serve as the primary point of contact for all plant quality initiatives, leading a skilled team and partnering cross-functionally with engineering, manufacturing, and supply chain to uphold product integrity and compliance standards.

The Quality Engineering Manager will report directly to the General Manager and play a key role in driving ISO certification, Lean initiatives, and process excellence across the facility.
Key Responsibilities
  • Lead and mentor the Quality Team; establish clear goals, KPIs, and accountability standards.
  • Utilize statistical and analytical tools (SPC, root-cause analysis, run charts, etc.) to identify and resolve quality issues.
  • Provide quality assurance support for new product launches, engineering changes, and technology implementations.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives across all manufacturing processes using Lean, Six Sigma, and theory-of-constraints principles.
  • Maintain and advance the plant's ISO-certified quality management system, ensuring compliance with internal and external requirements.
  • Manage product testing and evaluation for compliance with industry safety and performance standards (e.g., UL, CE, BHMA).
  • Collaborate with engineering to analyze part tolerances, recommend design enhancements, and ensure manufacturability.
  • Generate and implement quality improvement ideas; lead cross-functional problem-solving events.
  • Develop and maintain documentation such as control plans, work instructions, and inspection standards.
  • Promote a strong safety and quality culture across all levels of the organization.
Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree in Quality, Engineering, or a related technical field required.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience in manufacturing or industrial environments with emphasis on Quality Management and ISO systems.
  • Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) and/or Lean Six Sigma Green/Black Belt preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of SPC, FMEA, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement tools.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office and comfortable using data-driven quality systems.
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and analytical skills with the ability to influence across teams and levels.
  • Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.
  • Passion for driving results and improving systems through teamwork and accountability.
Why This Opportunity
This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated Quality professional to lead within a well-established, growing U.S. manufacturing operation that values innovation, safety, and employee development.

The company offers a collaborative environment, strong operational leadership, and the ability to make a measurable impact on plant performance and customer satisfaction.

description:

Join a Fortune 500 leader in the financial services industry during a period of major expansion and integration. Our client is a nationally recognized wealth management firm known for its award-winning advisor support, culture of compliance excellence, and continued growth through mergers and acquisitions. As part of a large-scale transition project, we’re hiring 20+ Supervisory Principals and Operational Specialists to support critical review and oversight functions in preparation for an upcoming platform conversion.

These fully remote contract roles offer competitive hourly rates, exposure to an enterprise-level compliance environment, and the opportunity to work with a respected industry leader recognized for stability, innovation, and long-term career development.
 

Position Overview

The Supervisory Principal team will play a key role in ensuring a smooth transition and maintaining the firm’s high standards of compliance oversight and advisor support. These professionals will be assigned to one of several key functional areas — Background Review, Outside Business Activity (OBA) Review, Advertising/Marketing Review, or Operations Support — depending on licensing and experience.

 

Key Responsibilities

Background Review (Approx. 5 positions)

  • Conduct comprehensive background reviews of financial advisors joining the platform

  • Investigate disclosures and assess potential compliance risks

  • Communicate findings and recommendations to internal stakeholders

  • Collaborate with advisor relations and compliance teams to resolve issues

Outside Business Activity (OBA) Review (Approx. 5 positions)

  • Review and evaluate advisors’ external business activities for potential conflicts of interest

  • Conduct due diligence and risk analysis aligned with firm and FINRA standards

  • Interact with advisors to clarify or document activity details

  • Prepare summaries and recommendations for compliance approval

Advertising/Marketing Review (Approx. 10 positions)

  • Review advisor advertising, websites, social media, and other marketing materials for compliance

  • Ensure content meets regulatory and firm branding standards

  • Partner with marketing teams and advisors to make compliant revisions

  • Provide subject-matter guidance on marketing and communications within a financial services context

Operational Specialist Roles (Approx. 3–4 positions, Non-Licensed)

  • Support core compliance operations including email monitoring, report distribution, and data validation

  • Perform administrative and investigative tasks supporting licensed teams

  • Handle credit pulls, mailbox management, and other operational functions to maintain workflow efficiency
     

Qualifications

For Licensed Supervisory Principal Roles:

  • Active FINRA Series 24 license required (must be current or within a two-year window of most recent firm registration)

  • Additional FINRA licenses (Series 7, 9/10, 63, or 65) preferred but not required

  • Experience in compliance, supervision, or advisor oversight within financial services

  • Strong investigative and analytical capabilities with sound regulatory judgment

For Advertising/Marketing Review Specialists:

  • Series 24 license required

  • Prior experience reviewing marketing or advertising materials in a financial or regulatory setting strongly preferred

  • Understanding of FINRA Rule 2210 and related advertising standards a plus

  • Ability to provide constructive compliance feedback in a collaborative, advisory tone

For Operational Specialist Roles (Non-Licensed):

  • Prior experience supporting compliance, operations, or risk functions in financial services preferred

  • Strong organizational and administrative skills

  • Proficiency with reporting tools, shared mailboxes, and general office technology

  • Ability to manage multiple workflows and deadlines

title: Lead SAP Architect
description:
Job Title: Lead SAP Architect
Salary range: $165K to $200K per year
Location: Denver, CO

Position Overview

We are seeking a visionary SAP Architect to lead the strategic design, governance, and continuous evolution of our SAP landscape. This role blends technical expertise with strategic thinking and innovation leadership, ensuring that SAP capabilities not only support but accelerate business transformation.

The SAP Architect will partner with business and IT leadership to define enterprise-wide SAP strategies, introduce emerging technologies, and deliver scalable, secure, and future-ready solutions that drive measurable business outcomes.

---

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

· Develop and maintain the SAP technology roadmap aligned with corporate strategy and enterprise architecture principles.

· Partner with the CIO, business leaders, and functional stakeholders to translate business vision into an SAP-enabled strategy.

· Lead SAP capability planning, investment decisions, and governance to maximize ROI.

Innovation & Transformation

· Drive the adoption of next-gen SAP capabilities including AI/ML, automation, and cloud-native services.

· Identify and pilot emerging SAP-related technologies to improve agility, user experience, and decision-making.

· Champion design thinking and innovation sprints to reimagine business processes using SAP as a platform for differentiation.

Solution Architecture & Delivery

· Architect end-to-end SAP solutions that integrate with enterprise platforms, ensuring performance, scalability, and security.

· Ensure designs adhere to architectural standards, best practices, compliance, and integration standards.

· Oversee SAP technical direction for major transformation programs, mergers/acquisitions, and global rollouts.

Collaboration & Influence

· Act as the primary thought leader and advisor on SAP capabilities for executives and stakeholders.

· Mentor technical teams, fostering a culture of innovation and continuous improvement.

· Build strong relationships with vendors, partners, and the SAP ecosystem to influence product roadmaps.

---

Qualifications

· Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field (Master's preferred).

· 10+ years in SAP solution architecture with deep expertise in S/4HANA and SAP Cloud offerings.

· Proven experience in enterprise architecture, strategy development, and innovation initiatives.

· Strong knowledge of integration frameworks, APIs, and data governance in an enterprise SAP context.

· Excellent communication and facilitation skills.
